newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soymeal, soyoil lower on new crop prospects.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soymeal, soyoil lower on new crop prospects.

text.p: CBOT soymeal and soyoil futures edged lower at midsession Friday, under pressure from good prospects for next year's soybean crop, traders said.
The soy products followed soybeans lower, as that market was pressured by weather.
Weather for the weekend is expected to be favorable for devlopment of the new crop. Forecasters see high temperatures in the 80s and 90s Fahrenheit and widespread rains.
Traders were also waiting for July options to expire at 1201 CDT. After expiry, the markets typically move to the most active strike prices.
Rumors that China bought 125,000 tonnes of U.S. soymeal for July/August delivery were greeted with skepticism by soymeal dealers and exporters offered no confirmation of the business.

In early soymeal trade, Griffin Trading sold 200 lots December, Cargill bought 100 July and LIT bought 100 December, pit traders said. In soyoil, ADM bought 100 August and Merrill Lynch and Prudential Securities each sold 100 December.
At 1120 CDT, July soymeal was down $3.50 at $270.40 and other months were down $1.00 to $2.30. July soyoil dipped 0.10 cent a lb to 22.94 cents and other months fell 0.10 to 0.20.
